html:
The Central American migrant caravans were large groups of people who walked together towards the United States from 2018. The best known set out from San Pedro Sula in Honduras on 13 October 2018.

San Pedro Sula had for years one of the highest murder rates in the world, driven by street gangs and drug trafficking. Poverty, the after-effects of Hurricane Mitch and the politics that followed the 2009 coup pushed many to leave Honduras. Travelling in thousands gave protection against robbery and kidnapping on the route through Guatemala and Mexico.

The caravans became a political issue in the United States, which pressed Mexico and Guatemala to stop them. Many migrants stayed in Mexico or waited at the border for years. Remittances from Hondurans abroad now make up about a quarter of the economy.
sum: The Central American migrant caravans were large groups of people who walked together towards the United States from 2018. The best known set out from San Pedro Sula in Honduras on 13 October 2018.
